## Open

### F-474 — The kustomize e2e asserted a pass's work before any pass read the switch

> _2026-10-10 · test/blong-int-kustomize · open_

Three CI runs read `0 obsolete, 0 deleted` from the operator and treated it as a prune that never
happens. Those passes were reconciling the declaration from _before_ the switch, because the runbook
applies the switched-off tree and asserts the operator's removal in the same run: the operator reads
the CR at the start of a pass, which is up to a resync interval later. The artifact settled it -
`status.deployments` still named mysql and the CR carried `services: {mysql: false}` two seconds
after that pass's own timestamp. The lesson is that a check of a reconciler's outcome has to wait
for the reconciler's precondition first, and to say which of the two it was waiting for; otherwise a
whole investigation chases a defect that no run has exercised.

### F-478 — Nothing applies a split tree's declaration, so the operator kept a stale one

> _2026-10-11 · test/blong-int-kustomize · open_

Moving the declaration to `example/` (D-507) took it out of every kustomization, and the runbook
that used to declare a suite by applying the tree stayed green: it applied base and overlay, the
pods rolled out, the login round trip answered, the exit code was 0. What it no longer did was tell
the operator what to run, so the operator reconciled the declaration an earlier run had left —
`spec.services: {mysql: false}` — and the run verified only the objects the tree itself carried. The
trail was in the cluster and nowhere in the log: the suite's Deployments had no `envFrom`, the
credentials Secret was missing from the tenant namespace, the reconcile line said
`obsolete: 7, deleted: 0` where a converging pass deletes. Read the CR's spec against what the
generation was given before trusting a green deploy.

### F-479 — A local cycle rewrites the committed tree, so the checkout is never clean

> _2026-10-11 · test/blong-int-kustomize · open_

The runbook's `TREE` defaults to the suite's committed `system/kustomize`, because that tree is the
runbook's own output and a reader compares it between revisions (D-475). A cycle that published an
artifact therefore leaves the base's templates with the concrete version where the committed form
has `PLACEHOLDER` — with no digest the version _is_ the artifact identity, so the placeholder rule
covers every occurrence of it — plus the digest and the spec hash in the example declaration. Two
files and a CR, on every run, in a tree whose committed form is the artifact-free one. Set
`TREE=/tmp/...` for a cycle whose point is verification.

### F-482 — A runbook variable that only worked when it was the default

> _2026-10-11 · test/blong-int-kustomize · open_

The runbook deletes its tree and applies its overlay, and both use `TREE` — but the generation it
runs between them never passed that path to the framework, so the two agreed only while `TREE` was
`system/kustomize`, the directory the CLI defaults to. Pointing it elsewhere emptied a path nobody
then wrote, and the apply answered that the directory does not exist after a generation that
reported success: a run whose point was to keep the checkout clean failed in the apply instead, and
the tree it _did_ write landed in the committed path, which is how a scratch run dirties the
repository. The output directory is an argument, and a variable that deletes and applies a path has
to be the one the generator is told to write — `suiteTreeGenerate` passes it now.

### F-483 — The deploy half of the runbook needs the suite's folder as its cwd

> _2026-10-11 · test/blong-int-kustomize · open_

`suite deploy --cluster=…` resolves its entry — `SUITE_ENTRY`, defaulting to `./index.ts` — against
the caller's working directory, and leaves the process there because the framework reads a package's
configuration relative to where it was started. Run from the repository root it asked the framework
for `/home/kalin/work/blong/blong/index.ts`, which does not exist:
`No entry point found in /home/kalin/work/blong/blong`, after the artifact had been fetched and the
tree written. The whole-run entry hides it because its machine half stands in the suite; the pattern
doc now says where to stand, and `SUITE_ENTRY` is the way to say it from elsewhere.

### F-614 — The migration check waited on the oldest failed attempt

> _2026-10-27 · test/blong-int-kustomize · open_

migrationStepRan took the first migrate-named Job from kubectl get jobs -o name, which is the oldest
attempt, and waited ten minutes on one that had already failed while the current attempt was
Complete. The run must pick the newest by creationTimestamp and hand kubectl the job.batch/name
spelling; the selection is now a pure latestMigrationJob with a no-cluster test.
